sections.html:
Two rivers meet at New Bern, and an old core sits beside newer subdivisions. That mix shapes what a quick sale looks like. Owners of historic or storm-worn houses often hit snags with lenders and inspectors, which is why many look at cash buyers who skip that process.

New Bern is the Craven County seat, with an estimated 34,724 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 29,524 in the 2010 census and 31,319 in April 2020. About 24.5% of residents are 65 or over. Heirs with a parent's house to clear, and retirees leaving for a family member's town, are common sellers, and each needs a firm closing day.

  • A retail listing fits a house in sound shape when the seller can sit through a buyer's loan process.
  • A cash sale fits a house with needed repairs, a renter inside or a date that cannot move.
  • Selling without an agent suits owners at ease with disclosure forms and contract drafting.

sections.h2: How New Bern homes are valued and rented
sections.html:
Homes that owners live in are worth a median of $240,100 in New Bern over 2020 to 2024, and 59.7% of the city's homes are owner-occupied. A downtown cottage or a house by the water will sit off that median.

New Bern housing and household figures, 2020-2024
MeasureNew Bern figure

Median household income$61,031
Average commute to work18.8 minutes

Monthly costs of ownership run $1,504 with a mortgage and $567 without, so carrying an empty house for months is a cost worth counting before you decide how long to wait.

If the house is in a historic district, the city requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before any exterior alteration, and buyers who plan visible changes will need to apply.

City staff can sign off on some work classed as in-kind replacement or minor, while the rest goes before the Historic Preservation Commission. The commission works from the Land Use Ordinance and its Historic District Guidelines, both linked from the city's HPC page, which also has an application, instructions and a worksheet.

That page also notes that old buildings on low, coastal ground are hard to keep up through severe storms, and it links a state preservation office video on getting ready and recovering. A listing that discloses the district and any past storm damage reads as straightforward to buyers.

  • Learn whether the parcel is mapped into a district before you set the price.
  • Mention the review requirement to buyers early.
  • Skip costly exterior repairs if you plan an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Craven County revaluation and the tax bill
sections.html:
Craven County appraises the parcel. A countywide revaluation for tax year 2028 is under way, and the previous one was finished in 2023. A comparable sales search will open in February 2028. Until then, the county tax department can give you the property card for your parcel. For a seller, the 2028 revaluation is mostly a talking point with buyers.

State rules fill in the rest. Bills are due September 1 and carry no interest until early January. Then a 2% charge applies, followed by three-quarters of a percent monthly from February. A value dispute goes first to the county's review board, and a further appeal to the Property Tax Commission has a 30-day window after the board mails its ruling.

Your closing attorney sets how the year's bill is split with the buyer.

Sellers pay the state's deed tax, $1 for each $500 of price, before recording. Filing starts at $26.00 for a general instrument. Recording a release of a paid-off deed of trust carries no fee.

Your closing attorney handles these payments. Call the Craven County register of deeds for office hours.

sections.h2: Tax exclusions that end with a sale
sections.html:
Older owners are a large part of the city, so this question comes up often. Three state programs exist, and each owner may use only one:

  • Seniors or disabled owners within the income cap can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value. The state printed a $38,800 cap for 2026.
  • A disabled veteran can exclude the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test on the state form.
  • A circuit breaker caps the tax at a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

When the house is sold, deferred circuit breaker taxes for the last three fiscal years come due, so have the Craven County assessor give you a figure ahead of closing.

sections.h2: What if a New Bern owner faces foreclosure?
sections.html:
The Craven County clerk of court hears foreclosures for New Bern houses. Once an auction sale is reported, ten-day periods open for higher bids. An owner who pays the loan off beforehand keeps any equity, so request a payoff figure and the case file first.

Selling before the auction leaves you in charge of price and timing. Bring the foreclosure notice to your first meeting with a closing attorney, and ask each buyer whether they can close before the hearing date.

Gather the deed, a loan payoff letter and the last tax bill, then set your latest acceptable closing date.

  • Confirm the district status of the address.
  • Walk the house and note roof, moisture and foundation concerns.
  • Request a few written offers and compare the amount each leaves after costs.
  • Ask the assessor whether a homestead exclusion on the parcel ends at sale.

The county offices can confirm what applies to your parcel.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal, so the sale avoids the repair demands that often follow one. That matters on an older New Bern house with an aging roof or moisture in the crawl space. You still need a clear title, a payoff letter and a deed the closing attorney can record.

Expect the offer to reflect the cost of repairs. Set it beside what a retail listing would leave after agent fees, repairs requested by a buyer's inspector and the months of carrying costs while you wait for a loan to be approved.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited New Bern house
sections.html: Heirs often sell a parent's house here. Before accepting any offer, confirm who has authority to sign. A closing attorney or the clerk of court can tell you whether the heirs may sign or whether a personal representative is needed. Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any mortgage statement, and ask the assessor whether an exclusion on the parcel ends when title moves.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Bern house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase damaged houses as they stand, and a retail listing works if you disclose the damage and expect credit requests.

faqs.q: Does New Bern require approval for exterior work in a historic district?
faqs.a: Yes. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for exterior changes, though staff can clear minor work.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Craven County?
faqs.a: The seller. The statute puts it on the transferor, at $1 per $500.

faqs.q: When does Craven County revalue next?
faqs.a: Tax year 2028 is the next revaluation, and the last was completed in 2023.

faqs.q: Can selling stop a foreclosure in New Bern?
faqs.a: Paying the loan off before the auction ends it. After an auction, upset bids can still arrive for ten days, so ask the clerk first.
